summary: Tested two new features on top of iteration_1 pass: (1) AUTO EMAIL on POST /api/leads for Prioritas A + target region, and (2) PROJECT MAP page /peta. Added 3 pytest cases (TestAutoEmail). Full regression suite: 26/27 passed. Frontend: login OK, nav-peta present between nav-crm and nav-notifikasi (order verified by top px 180/224/268), /peta renders Leaflet OpenStreetMap tiles with 11 CircleMarkers, tooltip shows developer name, popup shows developer/project/region/priority badge and 'Lihat Detail' button with data-testid map-detail-{id}. Clicking Lihat Detail opens the LeadDetailDialog (role=dialog) with full lead details.

minor.issue: Resend blocks marketing@properlead.id as 'undeliverable_recipient' in test env, so auto_emailed_to only contains super_admin. Backend logic and query are correct (log confirms send attempt); this is a Resend deliverability limitation of the demo domain, not a code bug.
Intermittent race in parallel test run: another worker creates a notification between mark-all and re-fetch, leading to unread==1. Not a real bug; test is order-sensitive under xdist.

action_items: (Optional) For deterministic test env, allow overriding auto-email recipients to delivered@resend.dev, or seed marketing user with a Resend-verified test address.
(Optional) Make TestNotifications.test_mark_read_and_all resilient to parallel test creation (isolate class, or assert unread <= 1).
critical_code_review_comments: notify_new_lead_email correctly gates on prioritas=='A' AND lokasi_target, matches spec.
auto_emailed_to returned in POST /api/leads response works and only includes successfully sent recipients (failures logged but not returned).
MapPage.js uses react-leaflet@5 with CircleMarker + Popup, proper data-testids project-map / map-marker-{id} / map-detail-{id} all present.
parseCoord() safely handles missing/malformed koordinat strings — lead with no coord is filtered out.
Center defaults to points[0] or [-3.4, 114.8]; for empty leads it still renders map — good UX.
Leaflet CSS is imported inside MapPage.js — works, but could also be added globally for reuse.

success_rate.backend: 96% (26/27) — 1 flaky race in parallel notif test
success_rate.frontend: 100% (nav, map render, markers, popup, detail dialog all verified)
